record.title: Zyphra reports hierarchical sparse attention results through 256K context
record.summary: A preprint introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which routes queries through a tree of compressed key summaries to select sparse attention keys. In author-run tests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, six-level routing reportedly scored 93.3% on RULER-13 versus 96.0% for dense attention while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache; the authors also report favorable comparisons with Minimax Sparse Attention on long-context retrieval. They did not release optimized kernels. Latency advantages beyond measured evaluation lengths, including at millions or billions of tokens, are model-based projections, and performance at those lengths remains unvalidated.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors posted arXiv:2610.42112v1 on 2026-10-30 describing Zyphra Hierarchical Attention, a tree-routed sparse-attention method.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, the authors report reasoning and agentic-coding scores near the dense-attention baseline and a 93.3% versus 96.0% score on RULER-13 for a six-level router while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache. In a LongBench v2 comparison, they report a 14-point advantage over Minimax Sparse Attention at a similar 1.1% decode-key share, despite using one-tenth of its training-token budget.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, optimized GPU-kernel latency or measured performance beyond 256K tokens; multi-million- and billion-token speed claims are roofline-model extrapolations, and the authors state evaluation quality at those lengths has not been validated.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent implementation or reproduction of the retrieval and reasoning results was checked.
End-to-end latency with optimized kernels and empirical accuracy beyond 256K are not established; longer-context speed results are modeled.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported long-context retrieval quality persists in optimized implementations, sparse hierarchical routing could change local inference design choices for long-context systems. Current importance is bounded by author-run tests through 256K and unmeasured latency projections.
limitations: All evaluation results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed.
The principal RULER sweep is measured at 64K, 128K and 256K; performance quality beyond 256K is not validated in the paper.
The paper does not release optimized GPU kernels. Million- and billion-token latency comparisons use a roofline model rather than measured end-to-end service.
Results include Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and a separate Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B conversion; broad model-family transfer is not established.

relationships.summary: A related sparse-attention development is tracked separately in the canonical LSA record. The papers describe different mechanisms and their reported results are not a matched comparison; this link does not imply relative superiority.

brief.summary: A preprint introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which routes queries through a tree of compressed key summaries to select sparse attention keys. In author-run tests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, six-level routing reportedly scored 93.3% on RULER-13 versus 96.0% for dense attention while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache; the authors also report favorable comparisons with Minimax Sparse Attention on long-context retrieval. They did not release optimized kernels. Latency advantages beyond measured evaluation lengths, including at millions or billions of tokens, are model-based projections, and performance at those lengths remains unvalidated.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report a 93.3% versus 96.0% RULER-13 score for a six-level Qwen3.6 router while attending to 1%–6% of KV cache, performance near dense attention on reasoning and agentic coding tasks, and a 14-point LongBench v2 advantage over MSA at similar 1.1% decode-key share. Latency advantages beyond measured runs are from a roofline model.
technical.compute_or_cost: Router distillation is reported on a frozen Qwen3.6 backbone using 4B tokens. The paper models latency but provides no optimized-kernel end-to-end serving measurements.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors published a detailed 43-page preprint and reported their evaluation protocol and results. Outcome measurements are not independently demonstrated.
technical.mechanism: ZHA recursively builds compressed summaries of key/value chunks into a tree. A query routes from upper levels toward selected leaves and performs full attention on the selected keys, with tree depth grown to seek subquadratic scaling.
technical.regime: Primary evaluation converts Qwen3.6-35B-A3B using frozen-backbone distillation on 4B tokens, with RULER retrieval evaluated at 64K, 128K and 256K across tree geometries; an additional Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B conversion is reported. No optimized kernels are released.
technical.strongest_baseline: Dense attention and Minimax Sparse Attention on the same Qwen3.6 backbone are reported; the MSA indexer uses 40B training tokens. Other model-family and production-serving comparisons are not established.

brief.title: Zyphra reports hierarchical sparse attention results through 256K context
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported retrieval quality and sparse selection hold across models and real serving, hierarchical routing could reduce the cost of attention at long contexts. Evidence is currently author-reported on a small set of backbones and measured tasks through 256K tokens; projected latency at much longer contexts is not an empirical result.

other.title: Latent Sparse Attention reports long-context attention speedups up to 10M tokens
other.summary: A preprint introduces Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries search cluster summaries rather than score every key. In author-run tests, its distilled form stayed near the tested model baselines at contexts up to 10M tokens and reduced attention-layer prefill and decode time substantially on two specific model families and H200/B300 hardware. The paper reports smaller end-to-end serving gains than the per-layer headline; its 100M-token result is an extrapolation. The linked implementation could not be accessed during this review, and no independent reproduction was performed.
